clue.text: Tinker a little, using starter only after car's repaired

indicators.note: the a and little pieces come after the repaired car letters in the answer
something repaired has been put back together, so the letters of the word before are rebuilt

parts.note: the letters of car's, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the word that precedes is used

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling with a car, only using the starter motor once it has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like the verb to fiddle about, but here it is the noun for a cheeky child; 'repaired' is the anagram signal and 'after' places the remaining pieces at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinker, in British usage, is a mischievous youngster, a little scamp or imp.

clue.text: Think twice about Bible class with son falling behind idiots

indicators.note: the son's letter drops in after the idiots, at the back

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject where the Bible is studied
asses are fools

explanation.surface: A scripture teacher reconsidering a class where one boy lags behind the dunces.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate a matter again is to consider it a second time, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: University dons huntin' marine creature

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the larger word wears the university letter inside it

parts.note: huntin' with a dropped g is a clipped searchin', looking for something

explanation.surface: Academics who go hunting for some sea animal, in the clipped speech of the country set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers, which fits 'University'; it is the verb to put on, so U goes inside SEARCHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny echinoderm living on the seabed is a sea animal, an example of the class.

clue.text: School of architecture academy runs up to about the last month

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letters sit up above the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the word to goes round the month letters

parts.note: December, the final month of the year, shortened to DEC

explanation.surface: An academy of architecture working right up to the end of December.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' sets the first two letters above the rest; 'about' wraps the word to round the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative style of the 1920s and 30s, a movement or school of design including architecture.

clue.text: They take you out on your birthday

definitions.text: They take you out on your birthday

parts.words: They take you out on your birthday
parts.note: not a party treat: these are the women who deliver the baby on the day you are born

explanation.surface: Friends treating you to a night out to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take you out' suggests a celebration, but the birthday meant is the actual day of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses who deliver babies literally bring a newborn out into the world on the day of birth.

clue.text: Eggheads showing foolish elitist leaning

indicators.note: the words are arranged in a silly, senseless way, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Intellectuals betraying a silly snobbish bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges the letters of ELITIST LEANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is informal for intellectuals, and the intellectual class as a group bears this name.

clue.text: Slough's moderate Tory followed by fifty plus

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the next ones

parts.note: a wet was a moderate Conservative opposed to Thatcher's hard line
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
and means plus, as in two and two

explanation.surface: A political sketch of a middle-of-the-road Conservative MP in the town of Slough, aged over fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a bog; the 's is 'is'. A WET was a moderate Tory of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or marshy hollow, a kind of boggy ground.

clue.text: Dash or run to be involved in the day victory came twice

indicators.note: the run letter is caught up inside the doubled letters
the day's letters are written two times

parts.note: VE Day, 8 May 1945, marked victory in Europe
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A soldier's memory of a frantic run on the day the war in Europe ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives VEVE; 'to be involved in' puts R in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of flair and spirited energy is a close synonym.

clue.text: Decorous meeting in Kent?

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A seemly, proper get-together in the English county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous behaviour is calm and dignified, a synonym for staid and proper.

clue.text: Official ghost writer's boss should be charitable

parts.note: public in the sense of state or official, as in public office
a spirit is a ghost
an editor, ED, directs the writers on a paper

explanation.surface: A ghostwriter grumbling that their employer ought to be more generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ghost writer' reads as one job, but the two words split between two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned for the community's welfare is generous and charitable in spirit.

clue.text: A constituent that's divorced?

parts.note: a part is a component or constituent

explanation.surface: Asking whether a voter in some electorate has split from a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' suggests a voter, but it is a component.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorced couples are separated, living away from one another.

clue.text: After reforming, turn out educated or self-taught?

indicators.note: once the letters are reformed into a new shape, the anagram is made

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a reformed character turns out schooled or self-taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reforming' rearranges TURN OUT into UNTUTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-taught had no formal teaching, never having had a tutor or instruction.

clue.text: Bizarre, retiring somewhere in California — blunder by you and me?

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a city in California
to err is to make a mistake
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A strange gaffe, on returning from a Californian spot, that we made ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses LA + ERR + US.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamlike and bizarre is weird in the manner of the Surrealist painters.

clue.text: Meadow pipit's home with the most slender dimensions

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
a pipit is a small bird, which lives in a nest

explanation.surface: A nature note on the smallest nest a meadow pipit builds.
explanation.walkthrough: A meadow pipit is a real bird, but 'Meadow' is LEA on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the slimmest, with least fat, is the superlative of thin and lean.

clue.text: They study some fish, little ones

parts.note: a school is a shoal of fish
children are little ones

explanation.surface: Pupils studying fish and their young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' and 'school' go together, which hides the fish sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at primary or secondary level are learners, the ones who study.

clue.text: Outbreaks of movie star Moore appearing in films like Exodus

indicators.note: the actress appears inside the films, so her name goes in them

parts.note: Exodus is a sweeping 1960 film, an epic
Demi Moore is an American film actress

explanation.surface: Demi Moore turning up in historical blockbusters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is the container signal. Exodus is Otto Preminger's 1960 widescreen epic.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread outbreak of disease is an epidemic, so these are outbreaks.

clue.text: Approved finale with men O'Connor maybe brought over

parts.note: an end is a finale
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British entertainer and TV host

explanation.surface: A grand final number with Des O'Connor and his men brought on, given approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' reverses DES into SED. Des O'Connor was a popular British singer and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign or back something is to give it approval, so endorsed equals approved.

clue.text: Club in Milan shifted painter to rendering

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club

indicators.note: the letters are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Milan football club transferring an artist to a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges PAINTER TO into PRETATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's rendering of a piece is their reading or version of it.

clue.text: Made of clay, shell-like article held up by knight

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the knight letter, supported by it

parts.note: shell-like is British slang for an ear, as in a word in your shell-like
the is the definite article
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A pottery shell-shaped object carried aloft by a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell-like' is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen pots are made of baked earth, fired clay.

clue.text: Acorn with slight mutation arising, my word, that's initially important

indicators.note: a small change to the letters, two being swapped, signals an anagram
in a down clue, arising means going up, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A botanist marvelling at an acorn with a small mutation emerging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with slight mutation' turns ACORN into ACRON, and 'arising' reverses MY into YM. 'my' looks like an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is a word formed from initial letters, so initials matter most.

clue.text: Listen, playing it adds the sparkle to Christmas

definitions.text: it adds the sparkle to Christmas

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: Telling someone to listen, as something festive is being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges LISTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery strands of metallic foil decorating trees bring festive glitter at Christmas.

clue.text: One guarantees being cool and confident, right?

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
sure means confident

explanation.surface: Someone checking that a person who stays calm and confident is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' suggests calm, but it is IN, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that underwrites risk promises payment against loss, offering a guarantee.

clue.text: Nebulous body, fighting between two sizes

indicators.note: the fighting goes between the two size letters

parts.note: S and M stand for small and medium clothing sizes
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A cloudy shape fighting its way between two clothing sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts WAR inside S and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense cloud of insects in flight is a vague, shifting mass, a hazy body.

clue.text: Partly explode prototype spinning missile

indicators.note: the run of letters turns round and is read backwards
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A prototype weapon that blows up partly as it spins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' picks ODEPROT from expLODE PROTotype and 'spinning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater weapon launched at ships is a self-propelled missile.

clue.text: As spy at GCHQ eats, twit occasionally drops food

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, so the rest is kept at regular intervals

explanation.surface: An intelligence officer at GCHQ eating, and a fool spilling some dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally drops' keeps the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on. GCHQ is the UK's signals intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strands of pasta are a staple Italian food.

clue.text: Collars — you probably have 20 of them

definitions.meaning: to collar a suspect is to arrest or catch them
a person has ten on the fingers and ten on the toes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Collars' looks like shirt necks but is the verb to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for catching or arresting someone, and also the horny plates on fingers and toes.

clue.text: Paper from Paris wraps a sparkling drink

indicators.note: the newspaper wraps itself round the letter, which goes inside

parts.note: Le Monde is a French daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A French newspaper used to wrap a bottle of fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wraps' puts A inside LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy lemon-flavoured soft drink is a sparkling beverage, in British usage.

clue.text: Commercial about poet's inspiration was funny

indicators.note: the commercial goes round the inspiration

parts.note: an ad is a television commercial
a muse inspires poets

explanation.surface: A television advert about a poet's muse that turned out comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; the definition works as the past tense, as in 'the joke amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke that entertained an audience was funny to them, the verb in its past tense.
